summary: U-BX Technology Ltd. (the “Company” or “UBXG”), an artificial intelligence-driven value-added services and products provider to insurance carriers, today announced the pricing of its initial public offering (the "Offering") of 2,000,000 ordinary shares
body_text: U-BX Technology Ltd. Announces Pricing of $10Million Initial Public Offering Rhea-AI Impact (Neutral) Rhea-AI Sentiment (Neutral) Tags IPO offering See more from StockTitan in Google Search and AI answers. Adds StockTitan as a preferred source · opens Google Add on Google 03/27/2024 - 05:00 PM BEIJING, March 27, 2024 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- U-BX Technology Ltd. (the “Company” or “UBXG”), an artificial intelligence-driven value-added services and products provider to insurance carriers, today announced the pricing of its initial public offering (the "Offering") of 2,000,000 ordinary shares (the "Ordinary Shares") at a public offering price of $5.00 per share (“Public Offering Price”) for total gross proceeds of $10,000,000, before deducting underwriting discounts and other offering expenses. The Ordinary Shares have been approved for listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market and are expected to commence trading on March 28, 2024, under the ticker symbol " UBXG ". The Offering is being conducted on a firm commitment basis. The Company has granted EF Hutton LLC (“EF Hutton”), the underwriter, an option to purchase up to an additional 300,000 Ordinary Shares at the Public Offering Price, less underwriting discounts, to cover the over-allotment option, exercisable within 45 days from the closing date of the Offering. The Offering is expected to close on or about April 1, 2024, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions. EF Hutton is acting as the sole bookrunner for the Offering. Ortoli Rosenstadt LLP is acting as U.S. counsel to the Company, and Winston & Strawn LLP is acting as U.S. counsel to EF Hutton, in connection with the Offering. The Company intends to use the proceeds from this Offering for 1) research and development (60%); 2) advertising and marketing (30%); and 3) general working capital (10%). The registration statement on Form F-1 (File No. 333-262412) relating to the Offering, as amended, was filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"), and was declared effective by the SEC on March 25, 2024. The Offering is being made only by means of a prospectus. Copies of the final prospectus related to the Offering may be obtained, from EF Hutton, Attn: Syndicate Department, 590 Madison Avenue, 39th Floor, New York, NY 10022, or via email at syndicate@efhutton.com or telephone at (212) 404-7002. About U-BX Technology Ltd. Headquartered in Beijing, UB-X Technology Ltd. is a provider of insurance technology in China. The Company focuses on providing value-added services using artificial intelligence-driven technology to businesses within the insurance industry. The Company’s services and products primarily include: 1) Digital promotion services. The Company helps institutional clients boost their social media visibility and generate revenue through consumer engagement and client promotions. 2) Risk assessment services. The Company has developed a unique algorithm named "Magic Mirror" that calculates payout risks for auto insurance coverage based on vehicle information. Insurance carriers purchase the personalized risk reports generated by the algorithm. Magic Mirror utilizes AI and optical character recognition technology to produce detailed risk assessments, including accident likelihood, potential claims, and estimated settlement amounts. and 3) Value-added bundled benefits to insurance carriers. title: 2024 GEWA | KinderCare Learning Companies
body_text: Early childhood education provider is one of only two companies worldwide that have currently received this recognition eight times; wins Gallup’s inaugural With Distinction award LAKE OSWEGO, ORE. — March 28, 2024 — KinderCare Learning Companies , a leading provider of early childhood and school-age education and care, proudly celebrates their eighth consecutive Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award (GEWA). KinderCare is one of just two companies worldwide that have currently received the honor eight years in a row and remains the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with this award. This award, given by Gallup, recognizes organizations for their ability to build engaged workplace where employees thrive and drive business outcomes. KinderCare is also one of five companies worldwide to earn Gallup’s inaugural Exceptional Workplace Award with Distinction. This is Gallup’s top recognition for thriving workplaces, awarded only to a select few organizations that not only meet rigorous standards of excellence, but truly place engagement at the center of their business strategy. “At KinderCare, we’ve been on a 12-year journey toward improving our engagement. We know our work is never done,” said Paul Thompson, President of KinderCare Learning Companies. “We recognize this work is critical to supporting our culture as a great place to work and also in our work to provide the best support to families and employers, organizations and schools that we partner with. We’re honored to earn the Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award for the eighth consecutive year.” KinderCare employs nearly 40,000 teachers and staff who provide early childhood education and care at more than 2,400 early learning centers and sites across the country. KinderCare provides all employees with competitive benefits, including a child care tuition benefit, and gauges family, employee and client (organizations and school district) engagement annually to help ensure we’re continuing to support our communities and employees in the best possible ways. According to Gallup, just 23 percent of employees worldwide are engaged in the company they work for, which means they are not only committed to their work, they also feel connected to their workplace and their company’s overall mission or goals. In the United States, only 33 percent of employees are engaged. Gallup research found highly engaged workers result in fewer negative outcomes and greater success for organizations. GEWA winners have 14 engaged employees for every one actively disengaged employee. Similarly, KinderCare has an employee engagement ratio that’s nearly seven times the rate in the U.S. and just over 11 times the global rate. “Congratulations to the 60 organizations that have redefined what it means to be a great place to work. Your commitment to creating environments where employees are listened to, valued and positioned to use their strengths every day is what sets you apart. Thank you for setting a new global standard in what it means to be a thriving workplace,” said Jon Clifton, Gallup chief executive officer. ### About KinderCare Learning Companies® A leading provider early childhood and school-age education and care, KinderCare builds confidence for life in children and families from all backgrounds. KinderCare supports hardworking families in 40 states and the District of Columbia with differentiated flexible child care solutions to meet today’s dynamic work environment: In neighborhoods, with KinderCare® Learning Centers that offer early learning programs for children six weeks to 12 years old and with Crème de la Crème School® , which offers a premium early education model using a variety of themed classrooms; For work, wherever employees work, offering customized employer-supported child care benefits at more locations than any other provider, and In local schools, with Champions® before and after-school programs. KinderCare programs meet the highest standards, validated by independent, third-party evaluation including: Gallup , measuring workforce engagement, National Association for the Education of Young Children , ensuring individual early learning center quality, Cognia , accreditation for before- and after-school programs BRIGANCE® and TerraNova® assessments of children’s academic progress and achievement, and WELL Health-Safety Rating™ , validating health and safety practices in our facilities. Headquartered in Lake Oswego, Oregon, KinderCare operates more than 2,400 early learning centers and sites. In 2024, KinderCare earned its eighth Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award – one of only two current organizations worldwide to achieve this milestone for eight consecutive years. To learn more, visit KC-Learning.com .

title: Tired of the same old routine, Bengaluru?
body_text: Not-so-usual things to do in Bengaluru! Break free from the monotony and include some excitement in your weekends. Get ready to shake things up because we’ve curated a list of not-so-usual activities that will transform your weekends from mundane to magical! From bouncing on trampolines to connecting with fellow bookworms, there’s something for everyone in the vibrant streets of Bengaluru. Embrace the Unusual Imagine, It’s a Saturday morning, and instead of scrolling through your phone or binge-watching yet another series, you’re soaring through the air at a trampoline park, shaping clay into a masterpiece at a pottery workshop, jamming Bollywood oldies with your guitar buddies or even experiencing the thrill of driving a fast go-kart. Sounds intriguing, doesn’t it? That’s the beauty of Bengaluru — a city brimming with unconventional activities just waiting to be explored. So, why settle for the ordinary when you can dive into the extraordinary? Let’s dive in and discover the hidden gems that make Bengaluru weekends truly special. Theatre, Open Mic & Pottery Clubs: Unleash Your Creativity In this city, creativity knows no bounds. Whether you’re a drama enthusiast, a poetry aficionado, or a budding artist, there’s a place for you to shine. Take Maati Sona , for example — a cosy pottery studio nestled in the heart of the city. Here, you can unleash your inner artist and sculpt your imagination into reality, one clay masterpiece at a time. From beginner workshops to advanced classes, there’s something for every skill level, making it the perfect place to nurture your creativity and explore a new hobby. Additionally, if you or your office wants to plan a team outing, suggest Clay Station , it’s the perfect place to host a corporate event with your colleagues and encourage all to get their hands dirty! And if the stage is calling your name, dive into the world of theatre and open mic nights, where you can showcase your talent and connect with like-minded individuals who share your passion for performance. It’s not just about the applause; it’s about the thrill of stepping out of your comfort zone and embracing the spotlight. Small World , is one such community where you’ll find like-minded people who provide you with a safe environment to try out your inner artist. Every weekend, regular events and workshops are happening across Bengaluru related to your hobbies, if you want to be regularly updated about all such creative events, make sure to join our Events & Networking Group in the Shelf Community! Trampoline Parks: Reach for the Sky Ever wondered what it feels like to defy gravity? Well, wonder no more because Bengaluru’s trampoline parks are here to make your bodies full of adrenaline! Take, for instance, Play Factory in Electronic City — a haven for adrenaline junkies and people who just want to jump around like babies and feel the nostalgia of the time when they were teenagers. Imagine bouncing to your heart’s content, feeling the dopamine rush as you soar high in the air. It’s not just a workout; it’s an exhilarating adventure that will leave you feeling rejuvenated and alive. And if you’re in the mood for some urban thrills coupled with some amazing window shopping with premium brands, head over to Sky Jumper in Garuda Mall, Ashok Nagar , where you can bounce your way to happiness amidst the bustling life in this city. Similarly, if you want to experience India’s largest trampoline park, Bounce, Orion Mall , Bengaluru is the place to be. Be a part of the global Freestyle movement inspiring all to move, connect, and develop as part of BOUNCE Tribe. Trust us, once you experience the joy of bouncing, you’ll wonder why you didn’t try it sooner! Community Meetups: Forge Connections, Make Memories People say that life is better when shared with others, and nowhere is that more true than in this city’s vibrant community scene. Whether you’re new to the city or simply looking to expand your social circle, community meetups offer the perfect opportunity to connect with like-minded individuals and forge meaningful relationships that last a lifetime. Take, for instance, WePlayBlr — a thriving community of fun people who come together every weekend to just chill, fool around, and relax together escaping from the constant hustle of the city. In case you are a sports freak but don’t want to indulge in regular training rather than casual fun sporting events, from cricket matches to skating clubs like Bengaluru’s Skating Club , there’s no shortage of fun activities to enjoy with new friends by your side. And if you’re craving a more intimate setting, check out MET (Mixer Eat Talk) , where you can participate in jamming sessions, speed dating events, and more. It’s not just about making friends; it’s about creating memories that will last a lifetime. Reading Clubs: Exchange & Discuss the Books you read! In a world filled with screens and distractions, there’s something truly magical about getting lost in a good book. In Bengaluru, book lovers are spoiled for choice when it comes to reading clubs and literary gatherings. Take HSR Read , for example — a cosy community of avid readers who meet regularly to discuss their latest literary discoveries and engage in thought-provoking debates. Whether you’re a die-hard bookworm or just looking to expand your reading horizons, HSR Read offers the perfect opportunity to connect with fellow bibliophiles and dive into the world of words. And who knows? You might just discover your new favourite author or spark a lifelong passion for reading. Apart from small communities like the above, many pan-India reading communities could provide you with an opportunity to meet more like-minded individuals and share your common interest in reading and books. Once such community is Cubbon Reads in Cubbon Park Bengaluru, they are active in 70+ cities as of now! Dive into the Unconventional In a city as dynamic as Bengaluru, weekends are meant to be savoured, not squandered. So why not step out of your comfort zone and embrace the unconventional? Whether you’re bouncing on trampolines, shaping clay into art, or connecting with new friends at a community meetup, there’s no shortage of exciting adventures waiting to be had. So, what are you waiting for? Grab your calendar, round up your friends, and embark on a weekend journey filled with laughter, discovery, and unforgettable memories. Because in Bengaluru, the possibilities are endless, and the adventures are waiting for you to dive in headfirst! We at Shelf are building up a community for all the lovely people living in Bengaluru where we are providing them with all the necessary resources that could help them live an eventful life in the city, be it from finding places to chill and hangout with new people or even going solo for fun activities like rock climbing and skateboarding. If you liked reading our blog & want to explore other hidden gems of the city: Join “The Shelf Community!”

title: Send logs to Grafana Loki with Rust
summary: Exploring how to send logs to a Grafana Loki instance using Rust, without Promtail
body_text: Hello world! We will look at how you can leverage Grafana Loki for log storage and analysis. Application monitoring tools are a crucial part of monitoring and observability. They allow you to examine exactly how your application works, what is going in/out, and what is going wrong. Using application monitoring tools saves time and money by being able to fix production issues faster and retaining users. At the end of this article, you'll have a Rust web service deployed freely to Shuttle that logs traces to Grafana. Interested in checking out the final repository? You can find that here. Why should I use Grafana Loki? # Loki is a logging service for Grafana designed with scalability and cost-effectiveness in mind. Rather than indexing the contents of your logs, it only stores the metadata and labels. A set of labels for each log stream is also used. Every unique set of labels represents each new stream - so if you add or remove any labels from a stream for example, you create an entirely new stream. With Grafana, you can also additionally visualize all of your data quite easily using either pre-created dashboards or making your own. Getting started # Pre-requisites # To get the most out of this article, you need to either self-host Grafana services or sign up to Grafana Cloud. For this article we'll mostly be referencing Grafana Cloud as this is the easiest way to use their services (without manual setup). To get started, you will want an API token that has the write:logs permissions. This can be done from Grafana Cloud user management. Make sure you save your Grafana user and API token variables, as you'll need them in just a little bit. For initializing our service, we'll use shuttle init --template axum (requires cargo-shuttle installed) to create a new Shuttle project with the Axum template. We will then add the following dependencies with this shell snippet: cargo add url cargo add tracing-subscriber -F fmt,env-filter cargo add tracing-loki cargo add tracing cargo add base64 cargo add shuttle-runtime --no-default-features We'll also additionally need to add the #[shuttle_runtime::Secrets] annotation macro to our main function. This allows us to automatically grab secrets from our Secrets.toml file when we use shuttle run to run our Shuttle service. It should look like this: [ .. ] use shuttle_runtime :: SecretStore ; #[shuttle_runtime::main] async fn main ( #[shuttle_runtime::Secrets] secrets : SecretStore ) -> shuttle_axum :: ShuttleAxum { let router = Router :: new ( ) . route ( "/" , get ( hello_world ) ) ; Ok ( router . into ( ) ) } The Secrets.toml file will be located at the project folder root and takes a key-value format. GRAFANA_USER = "<your-grafana-user-here>" GRAFANA_API_KEY = "<your-grafana-api-token-here>" Building # To get started, we will be using the tracing_loki crate to build the base of our tracing subscriber. tracing_loki allows us to create a tracing_subscriber layer that collects and exports logs to a Grafana Loki instance. On creation of a Grafana Cloud account we are given a free data source by default for Loki, which tracing_loki is compatible with. The default Grafana data source uses the basic authentication scheme, which you can find more about here. Later on when we create the tracing_loki tracing layer, we will add this as a HTTP header. We'll start by grabbing our secrets and making a Base64 string out of them: fn init_grafana_subscriber ( store : SecretStore ) { let grafana_user = store . get ( "GRAFANA_USER" ) . unwrap ( ) ; let grafana_password = store . get ( "GRAFANA_API_KEY" ) . unwrap ( ) ; let basic_auth = format! ( "{grafana_user}:{grafana_password}" ) ; let encoded_basic_auth = BASE64_STANDARD . encode ( basic_auth . as_bytes ( ) ) ; // .. rest of code } Next, we'll need to create the tracing_loki layer which sends the logs to a Grafana instance. A few things are going on in the below snippet: We add a label (with a key and a value) We add an extra field for the Process ID (PID). This also takes a key-value format, so if you wanted to add anything else, you would do it here. We set the HTTP header using the .http_header() function, setting the Authorization header as required. use url :: Url ; let url = Url :: parse ( "https://logs-prod-012.grafana.net" ) . expect ( "Failed to parse Grafana URL" ) ; let ( layer , task ) = tracing_loki :: builder ( ) . label ( "application" , "shuttle-grafana" ) . unwrap ( ) . extra_field ( "pid" , format! ( "{}" , process :: id ( ) ) ) . unwrap ( ) . http_header ( "Authorization" , format! ( "Basic {encoded_basic_auth}" ) ) . unwrap ( ) . build_url ( url ) . unwrap ( ) ; Additionally, we will want to create an EnvFilter . Having the tracing subscriber set at the default trace logging level can be useful. However, due to parsing headers and other similar actions that all use trace! spans, there are quite a lot of them. This can lead you to go over the free tier limits unintentionally. Here, we will set the default directive so that we only get errors where the logging level is DEBUG or above (i.e. warning or an error). use tracing_subscriber :: filter { EnvFilter , LevelFilter } ; let filter = EnvFilter :: builder ( ) . with_default_directive ( LevelFilter :: DEBUG . into ( ) ) . parse ( "" ) . unwrap ( ) ; The last thing to do is to create a tracing subscriber with the layers that we've created, and then initialise it! You may have noticed earlier that the tracing_loki::builder() method also generates a task that deals with log aggregation. We will need to spawn a Tokio task to handle this. // We need to register our layer with `tracing`. tracing_subscriber :: registry ( ) . with ( filter ) . with ( tracing_subscriber :: fmt :: Layer :: new ( ) ) . with ( layer ) // One could add more layers here, for example logging to stdout: // .with(tracing_subscriber::fmt::Layer::new()) . init ( ) ; // The background task needs to be spawned so the logs actually get // delivered. tokio :: spawn ( task ) ; Now the function is done! We can add it to our fn main at the start of the function. #[tracing::instrument] async fn hello_world ( ) -> & 'static str { tracing :: debug! ( "An event happened!" ) ; "Hello, world!" } #[shuttle_runtime::main] async fn main ( #[shuttle_runtime::Secrets] secrets : SecretStore ) -> shuttle_axum :: ShuttleAxum { setup_tracing ( & secrets ) ; let router = Router :: new ( ) . route ( "/" , get ( hello_world ) ) ; Ok ( router . into ( ) ) } When using shuttle run now, your terminal will become populated with traces. If you visit localhost:8000 in the browser, you should see a debug tracing event with the description An event happened! in your traces. Note that it may take Grafana 5-10 minutes to receive your traces. Reading your logs # To read your logs, you need to create a dashboard for your data source. Head over to your Grafana Cloud instance, find the Grafana Cloud data source and create a dashboard for it. Then once you're on the dashboard, you can query your logs! A best practices guide for building Grafana dashboards can be found here . The label we added to our logs should show up under the Labels column. It will contain the extra label we put in (the application label), as well as the logging level of the trace. The trace will also contain exactly what was in the trace message. If you need to add fields in the #[tracing::instrument] macro, you can do so and it will show up in Grafana. You can also find a guide for understanding labels here. Deploying # To deploy, simply use shuttle deploy and watch the magic happen! Finishing up # Thanks for reading! Application monitoring is just one step to ensuring our Rust web services are performing better than ever. By using instrumentation, we can reduce the need for manual debugging. Read more: Read our guide to the tracing libraries Send logs to Datadog with Rust 8 tools to help you be more productive with Rust

title: Classic Homemade Egg Yolk Pasta Recipe
summary: Looking for a top-notch egg yolk pasta recipe? Read our blog to learn how to make egg yolk pasta and get expert tips for cooking the perfect dish. ✓ Click here!
body_text: Rich, golden, and irresistibly smooth—egg yolk pasta dough is more than just a meal; it’s a canvas for culinary artistry. Whether you’re coating it with a fiery Arrabiata sauce or embracing simplicity with a classic cacio e pepe, the true measure of a pasta dish always comes back to the quality of its dough. Mastering the art of homemade egg yolk pasta is surprisingly easy. It promises to elevate any pasta dish from simple to sublime and start you on a journey through the rich traditions of Italian cuisine. Before we get cooking, let’s dig into what makes this dough so delectable. The Benefits of Adding Egg Yolks to Pasta If a simple dough of flour, water, and salt will do, why are egg pasta dough recipes favored by home and pro chefs alike? Eggs bring more than personality to the pasta party. Some other benefits they bring to your dough include: Adding a Nutritional Boost Egg yolks are brimming with nutrients. They contain high amounts of vitamin A, which supports a healthy immune system, and vitamin B12, which promotes the production of red blood cells in the body. Egg yolks are also an excellent source of essential minerals like potassium, zinc, and calcium. Embracing egg yolks in your pasta enriches its flavor profile and adds some protein for a more balanced meal. Pair your pasta with veggies or heart-healthy olive oil, and you’re well on your way to taking the guilt out of your pasta pleasure. Improves the Workability of the Dough Egg yolks enrich your dough with a rich, velvety texture, adding moisture and suppleness that make it easier to knead and shape. As the yolks coat the flour, they create a luxurious, elastic texture that rolls out effortlessly for easy cutting and molding, making the process easier and more enjoyable for pasta enthusiasts and novices. Infuses Dough with a Luxurious Flavor Egg yolk pasta is renowned for its rich, creamy taste and ability to elevate the most humble pasta dish into an indulgent comfort food experience. Top chefs recommend making homemade pasta with egg yolks because it adds a richness that transcends ordinary pasta recipes. No Pasta Machine Required Egg yolks enhance your dough’s malleability, making it a breeze to roll and shape by hand. Set aside the pasta machine and embrace the tactile pleasure of forming your pasta by hand. With the right egg-yolk pasta ratio, you’ll be able to effortlessly roll the pasta thin and even, proving that the best tools are right at your fingertips. Improves Sauce Adhesion The fat content from egg yolks and additional protein changes the surface texture of pasta to allow the sauce to grip better. When your sauce effectively clings to your pasta, every bite is full of flavor. Lends a Silky Finish to Your Pasta Egg yolk pasta strikes the ideal balance between a firm bite and a tender texture. The cooked pasta will perfectly absorb sauces and hold its shape, making it the perfect foundation for all your favorite dishes, from carbonara and pesto to alfredo and bolognese. 10 Types of Pasta Well Suited for Egg Yolk Pasta Dough Now that you’re confident about embarking on your journey to egg yolk pasta mastery, the next thing to do is decide which pasta shape you should make! The good news is, there are no rules! You can make a myriad of different kinds of pasta with your egg-based dough. Although strict culinary experts might recommend matching specific pasta doughs to the perfect shape for the adventurous home cook (and many rising stars in the restaurant world), the pasta-bilities for using egg yolk pasta dough are endless! Try your hand at some of these popular pasta shapes: 1. Fettuccine The richness of egg yolks adds a velvety texture to fettuccine, creating a luxurious mouthfeel that pairs perfectly with creamy alfredo sauces. Plus, egg yolks give each long and elegant strand a silky consistency and beautiful golden hue. 2. Ravioli For filled pasta like ravioli, you need a dough that’s strong but not tough. Egg yolk pasta hits the mark, offering a tasty and reliable foundation for all your favorite fillings, whether meat, cheese, or vegetables. 3. Lasagne Few dishes are more synonymous with rich, hearty flavor than lasagne. It’s the ultimate Italian comfort food, and for good reason— it’s a meal that truly warms the soul. With a well-balanced egg yolk-to-flour ratio pasta, you can level up your lasagne game to achieve satisfying and sumptuous layers of texture that fill your belly and delight your senses. 4. Tagliatelle Tagliatelle is similar to fettuccine but has wider, flatter strands that deliver more surface area for absorbing sauce. Adding egg yolks to tagliatelle dough elevates its tender texture to showstopper status, making it the star of any dish. 5. Tortellini Tortellini is known for its tiny, circular shape, which enfolds any number of flavorful fillings. The intricate folds capture and hold your sauce, offering the perfect bite every time. The trick with tortellini is to roll the dough into a thin sheet so the folded shape is tender, not tough. Egg yolk pasta dough is perfectly suited for the task — flexible enough to roll out thin and strong enough to hold its shape in boiling water. 6. Orecchiette Making orecchiette may be the most impressive of all the ways to put an egg yolk pasta dough recipe to good use. This pasta shape is less well-known than conventional options like lasagne or fettuccine, making it a conversation starter at any dinner party. Plus, its bowl-like contours are well-suited to show off your favorite sauce. The richness of egg yolks intensifies the luxurious mouthfeel of this pasta and pairs beautifully with bechamel sauce. 7. Cannelloni Imagine large, tube-shaped pasta filled with savory ingredients such as ricotta cheese or minced beef, all nestled under a tangy red sauce. This dish truly showcases the versatility of egg yolk pasta, showing off its tender yet robust texture to beautifully complement your favorite filling. 8. Farfalle Also known as bow-tie pasta, farfalle is traditionally served in a cream-based sauce but also makes a fantastic addition to soups or pasta salads. Egg yolks give these bow ties a vibrant golden hue and help them hold up to hearty sauces. But remember to let your fresh farfalle dry for at least 30 minutes before you cook it to keep them from sticking together and guarantee an even cook. 9. Pappardelle Pappardelle is a broad, flat pasta ribbon, similar to fettuccine but about twice the width. These noodles provide the ideal surface area for clinging coverage from rich, robust sauces, such as meaty ragus or creamy mushroom sauces. The hearty texture of pappardelle, especially when made from egg-yolk pasta dough, provides a satisfying bite that complements a substantial sauce. The richness of the egg yolk in the pasta dough deepens the pasta’s flavor, making it a perfect pairing for the intensity of slow-cooked meat sauces. 10. Capellini By contrast, capellini, or angel hair pasta, is a very thin pasta that cooks quickly, making it an excellent choice for light and delicate sauces. Because of its fine nature, capellini pairs well with smooth tomato-based sauces, light vegetable broths, or simple oil-based dressings. The delicate structure of capellini made from egg-yolk pasta dough brings a subtle richness and a silky texture to a dish without overpowering the flavors of the sauce. The egg yolk adds a level of refinement and depth to the pasta, balancing perfectly with light and elegant sauces. Classic Egg Yolk Pasta Recipe Egg yolk pasta brings a rich flavor and tender texture to your pasta dishes. Try this recipe for the ideal flour-to-egg yolk ratio for pasta. It’s the perfect way to start cooking pasta from scratch and enjoy the luxurious taste of fresh pasta at home. Here’s a simple pasta recipe with egg yolks that makes approximately four (4) servings. Ingredients: 2 cups (240g) All-Purpose Flour, plus extra for dusting 6 large Egg Yolks 1 whole Egg 1 teaspoon Olive Oil 1 teaspoon Salt Water, as needed Instructions: Prepare the Dough On a clean, flat surface, create a mound with the 2 cups of flour and make a well in the center. Add the egg yolks, whole egg, olive oil, and salt into the well. Mix the Ingredients Using a fork, gently beat the eggs, olive oil, and salt together, gradually incorporating the flour from the sides of the well. Continue until the mixture starts to form a sticky dough. Knead the Dough With floured hands, start kneading the dough, incorporating more flour as needed to prevent sticking. Knead for about 10 minutes or until the dough is smooth and elastic. If the dough is too dry, add a few drops of water. The final dough should be firm and not sticky. Rest the Dough Shape the dough into a ball and wrap it in plastic wrap. Let it rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes. This resting period allows the gluten to relax, making the dough easier to roll out. Roll Out the Pasta After resting, divide the dough into four equal portions. Work with one portion at a time, keeping the others covered to prevent drying. Flatten the dough into a disk with your hands, then use a pasta machine or a rolling pin to roll out the dough into thin sheets, aiming for a thickness of about 1-2 mm. Lightly flour the dough as necessary to prevent sticking. Cut the Pasta Once the dough is rolled out, you can cut it into your desired shape, like fettuccine, tagliatelle, or lasagna sheets. If using a pasta machine, use the cutter attachment. If cutting by hand, lightly flour the pasta sheet, roll it loosely, and slice it into strips with a knife. Cook the Pasta Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta in batches to prevent sticking, stirring occasionally, for 2-3 minutes or until al dente. Remember, fresh pasta cooks much faster than dried pasta. Serve Drain the pasta and serve it immediately with your favorite sauce. title: Women in Tech Meetup

body_text: Learning about risk-taking, sentiment analysis, cybersecurity, and psychological safety in one evening? That’s quite a mix, isn’t it? That’s what the audience got offered at the Women in Tech meetup, which took place on February 29th in trivago’s office space. Together with iteratec, trivago had the pleasure of bringing together the vibrant community of female tech talents and their allies on the occasion of International Women’s Day, for an evening featuring stories about risk, safety, and continuous improvement. Aida Orujova and Sophia Breth guided the crowd through the evening in which 60 guests listened to four talks on a diverse set of topics: Andrea Fernandez : Unleashing the power of risk-taking Andrea opened the evening with her perspective, recommending everyone to take calculated risks in both professional and personal lives. According to her, calculated risk-taking can greatly accelerate progress. The key is to learn fast from mistakes and to incorporate acquired knowledge into the future actions. Lucia Leardini : The Language of Lodging - A sentimental journey through accommodation reviews Lucia shared with us her first application of sentiment analysis on hotel review data. She compared the performance of VADER and TextBlob with a dataset of hotel reviews, with VADER slightly outperforming TextBlob in this context. Overall, she states that sentiment analysis has a lot of potential, but it also requires quite a deep dive into modeling, data structure, and theoretical foundation. A natural next step would be to benchmark tested libraries with GPT solutions. Elke Hiendl : Redefining Cybersecurity - Beyond Tech to Culture and Awareness Elke introduced us to the world of cybersecurity and all its aspects. She highlighted that there’s way more than “just” passwords and how most of cybersecurity issues are not about hacking computers, but hacking human brains. She underlined that it requires the right mindset and culture to safeguard our digital spaces. Michael Thiel : The importance of psychological safety in teams Michael closed the round of talks by sharing his experience on psychological safety in teams. With his background as a psychologist, he shared his best practices on how to create a safe space in teams. He guided the audience through the theoretical foundation and how it can be applied in real life. His first tips were “share something personal… to show that you are human” and “make a joke (if you can)…because laughter works against stress and anxiety”, which he applied to his talk as well. Besides the talks, everyone had the chance to network over some food and drinks, creating a comfortable atmosphere to exchange on the topics presented by our speakers and beyond. We want to thank our colleagues at iteratec for the great collaboration in organizing the “Women in Tech” meetup! We’re looking forward to the next edition 🙌 About the speakers: Andrea Fernández, trivago Andrea leads the Data Intelligence team at trivago. Data Intelligence aims to enable other teams to make data-driven decisions. Andrea completed a PhD in mathematics in the UK and has been working since then with marketing, bidding, prediction, and ranking algorithms, among others. She is eager to share her experience and learnings on leading data teams. Beyond her impactful role, Andrea is also a member of trivago’s FAME (Female Ambassadors and Mentors in Engineering) group, an initiative whose goal is to inspire, empower, and attract women to the tech field. Lucia Leardini, trivago Lucia is a Senior Data Scientist in the B2B Ventures team at trivago. After a PhD and post-doc in Physics at the Ruprecht-Karls-Universität in Heidelberg, Lucia was part of the trivago Marketplace, working with the Auction algorithm and with market and advertisers’ dynamics. She recently moved to the B2B team, taking care of alternative revenue streams and third-party data exchange. Lucia is also a member of trivago’s FAME (Female Ambassadors and Mentors in Engineering) group, an initiative whose goal is to inspire, empower, and attract women to the tech field. Elke Hiendl, iteratec After completing her studies in biology and conducting basic research in molecular neurobiology, Elke switched to IT and began her career as a system and network administrator. She later assumed the position of data protection officer for the company and gradually shifted her focus to IT security. Michael Thiel, iteratec Michael has been working as a psychologist, therapist and coach for more than 35 years. He works as a psychological coach and supervisor in hospitals, media companies and in the IT sector.

title: Portabilidade numérica para empresas
summary: Guia rápido de portabilidade numérica para empresas: processo seguro com confirmação por SMS. Transição eficiente sem perder números.
body_text: A portabilidade numérica para empresas é um processo que permite aos usuários de telefonia manter seus números de telefone ao mudar de operadora. Recentemente, esse processo passou por uma atualização importante para aumentar a segurança dos consumidores, para redução dos golpes de SIM SWAP. A partir de 08 de Janeiro de 2024, as linhas de celular PJ (Pessoa Jurídica), possuem um novo requisito: a confirmação da portabilidade por SMS. Este artigo detalha o procedimento atualizado para realizar a portabilidade de números de celular para empresas, usando como referência as novas regras divulgadas. Solicitação da Portabilidade para empresas O primeiro passo no processo de portabilidade para empresas é a solicitação. Isso pode ser feito de maneira conveniente através do Dashboard da Salvy ou pelo aplicativo. Essa flexibilidade permite que os responsáveis pelas decisões nas empresas escolham o método mais adequado para suas necessidades, facilitando o início do processo de portabilidade. Assim, lembre-se de checar se suas linhas não possuem um contrato de fidelidade com a operadora de origem. Prazo para Portabilidade para empresas Após a solicitação, a portabilidade será realizada em até 72 horas úteis. Este prazo é crucial para as empresas planejarem qualquer comunicação necessária com clientes ou parceiros durante a transição, garantindo uma mudança suave sem perda de conectividade. Confirmação via SMS A nova etapa no processo de portabilidade é a confirmação via SMS. Um SMS de confirmação será enviado ao chip atual, e é fundamental manter o chip atual ativo até a conclusão do processo. Para prosseguir com a portabilidade, o cliente deve responder com “SIM” ao SMS recebido. Este SMS será enviado do número 7678. Caso não receba, é aconselhável verificar se o número está bloqueado no aparelho. Exceções para Confirmação por SMS Existem exceções para a regra de confirmação por SMS. Para solicitações de mais de 5 portabilidades dentro de 24 horas, a confirmação por SMS não é necessária. Isso facilita o processo para empresas que precisam migrar vários números simultaneamente, tornando a transição mais eficiente. Após a Resposta do SMS Após a resposta ao SMS de confirmação, independente da resposta, um SMS será enviado ao cliente informando que a resposta está sendo processada. Se por algum motivo o cliente optar pelo cancelamento após ter respondido “SIM”, isso é possível até 1 dia útil antes da janela de portabilidade. Além disso, uma resposta “NÃO” coloca a solicitação em conflito por até 30 dias, oferecendo tempo para reconsideração ou resolução de quaisquer problemas. Conclusão A portabilidade numérica para empresas agora requer uma etapa adicional de confirmação por SMS, visando aumentar a segurança e a eficácia do processo. Compreender este procedimento e as suas nuances é essencial para as empresas que desejam mudar de operadora sem perder seus números de contato valiosos. Ao seguir este guia passo a passo, as empresas podem garantir uma transição suave e sem interrupções, mantendo a continuidade dos negócios e a satisfação do cliente. Portanto, este procedimento atualizado reflete o compromisso contínuo com a melhoria da experiência do cliente e a proteção contra fraudes, garantindo que a portabilidade numérica seja uma opção segura e confiável para empresas de todos os tamanhos.

title: Computer Aided Design (CAD): Definition, Types and Use
summary: CAD modeling is a revolutionary technology that improves the design process in various industries by providing better visualization of modeled components. Learn more about it here.
body_text: What Are Examples of Computer Aided Design in Real Projects? Examples of Computer Aided Design in real projects are listed below. Architectural Building Design (Houses, Skyscrapers, Floor Plans) : Architects use CAD to produce complete building documentation, including floor plans, elevations, sections, and roof layouts for residential homes and high-rise structures. A detailed floor plan for a 50-story commercial tower contains thousands of annotated elements (walls, doors, windows, stairwells, electrical symbols) all placed and dimensioned within a single coordinated CAD file. The drawings communicate construction intent to structural engineers, contractors, and building inspectors throughout the project lifecycle. Mechanical Parts Design (Gears, Engines, Machine Components) : Mechanical engineers model individual parts (spur gears, crankshafts, bearing housings, valve bodies) in 3D CAD with exact tooth profiles, bore dimensions, and surface finish callouts. An involute gear tooth profile generated in CAD is accurate to within 0.005 mm, supporting mesh quality requirements that manual drafting does not reliably achieve. The models feed into manufacturing drawings and CNC machining programs. Automotive Design (Car Bodies, Chassis, Engine Systems) : Automotive designers use surface modeling CAD to define exterior body panels with Class-A surface quality, while structural engineers model chassis frames and suspension geometry in solid modeling environments. A full vehicle CAD assembly contains over 30,000 individual part files linked in a managed product data environment. Crash simulation, aerodynamic analysis, and packaging studies all reference the CAD geometry before physical prototypes are built. Aerospace Engineering (Aircraft Wings, Fuselage Structures) : Aerospace CAD models define wing airfoil profiles, spar geometry, fuselage frame spacing, and skin panel contours to tolerances measured in thousandths of an inch. A commercial aircraft wing model contains hundreds of structural components whose geometry is validated in the CAD environment against Federal Aviation Administration structural certification requirements. Electrical Circuit Design (PCB Layouts, Wiring Systems) : Electrical CAD software places components (resistors, capacitors, ICs, connectors) on printed circuit board layouts and routes copper traces at widths from 0.1 mm to several millimeters, depending on current capacity. The completed PCB layout exports as Gerber files that go directly to board fabrication equipment. Civil Engineering Projects (Bridges, Roads, Drainage Systems) : Civil engineers use CAD to design road alignments, bridge deck geometries, drainage networks, and site grading plans that define earthwork volumes and stormwater flow paths. A highway interchange design in CAD integrates alignment data, grade profiles, cross-sections, and drainage structures into a coordinated documentation set. Product Design (Furniture, Appliances, Consumer Electronics) : Industrial designers model furniture joints, appliance housings, and consumer device enclosures in CAD, combining aesthetic surface modeling with structural solid geometry to meet visual and functional requirements. 3D Printing Models (Prototypes, Custom Parts) : CAD models exported as STL or 3MF files feed directly into 3D printing slicing software, translating digital geometry into layer-by-layer build instructions for FDM, SLA, and SLS printers. Interior Design Layouts (Room Planning, Furniture Placement) : Interior designers use 2D and 3D CAD tools to plan room layouts, place furniture to scale, and visualize spatial relationships before physical arrangements are finalized. Medical Device Design (Prosthetics, Implants) : Biomedical engineers use CAD to model prosthetic limbs, orthopedic implants, and surgical instruments with anatomical geometry defined to tolerances as tight as 0.01 mm, meeting FDA and ISO 13485 design documentation requirements. How are CAD Drawings Used in Construction and Manufacturing? CAD drawings are used in construction and manufacturing as the authoritative reference documents that define what is built, how it is built, and to what specification. A set of CAD-produced architectural and structural drawings specifies wall dimensions in construction, foundation depths, steel member sizes, and connection details that every trade on the job site follows. The drawings carry dimension strings, material callouts, and detail references that eliminate interpretive ambiguity during fabrication and installation. CAD drawings define part geometry through orthographic views, section cuts in manufacturing, and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) callouts that machinists and quality inspectors use as the production standard. A machined aluminum bracket drawing, for example, specifies hole diameters, thread forms, flatness tolerances, and surface roughness values that the CNC operator programs from the document. The drawing serves as the inspection reference, allowing quality teams to verify finished parts against the original design intent. Without CAD-produced drawings, production consistency across multiple machines, shifts, and supplier facilities is difficult to maintain. Are CAD Drawings Required for Production? Yes, CAD drawings are required in many industries and workflows, but some modern manufacturing environments use 3D model-based definitions (MBD) instead of traditional drawings. Drawings provide the detailed technical instructions that operators, machinists, and fabricators need to produce parts and structures that meet design specifications consistently across multiple production runs. These standards require controlled design documentation and traceability, but documentation may include drawings, digital models, specifications, or other controlled records. In commercial construction, building permits require stamped CAD-produced drawings submitted to local authorities before work begins. A purchase order without a drawing or model file lacks the dimensional and material data needed to quote, set up machines, or inspect finished parts in contract manufacturing. Verbal descriptions and sketches fail to convey the tolerances, surface finishes, and material specifications in precision manufacturing. CAD drawings close that gap by encoding design intent in a universally readable technical format accepted across industries and international supply chains. How Does Revit compare to AutoCAD in CAD Workflows? Revit, compared to AutoCAD in CAD Workflows shows a clear difference in how each system handles design, data, and coordination. Revit focuses on building information modeling while AutoCAD focuses on drafting and documentation, and the two platforms serve fundamentally different workflow structures despite both carrying the CAD classification. Revit constructs an intelligent 3D building model where walls, floors, roofs, and structural members are data-rich objects that carry properties (material, thickness, fire rating, cost) beyond simple geometry. AutoCAD, by contrast, produces drawings composed of lines, arcs, and text that communicate design intent without the embedded data layer that Revit maintains. The practical difference affects how teams work and how information flows across a project. A change made to a wall in Revit updates the floor plan, section, elevation, and schedule simultaneously because all views derive from a single model. The same change in AutoCAD requires manual updates across each affected drawing sheet. For multi-discipline building projects where architecture, structure, and mechanical systems must coordinate, the data-driven model approach that distinguishes Revit® Vs. AutoCAD® determines which platform better fits the project's collaboration and documentation requirements. What Makes Revit Different From AutoCAD in Design Use? Revit differs from AutoCAD in design use by focusing on intelligent modeling instead of basic drafting. Revit creates intelligent 3D building models where every element is a parametric object with embedded data, while AutoCAD creates drawings composed of geometric entities without the same level of embedded building information. A wall placed in Revit knows its height, material, thermal resistance, and structural load-bearing status. A wall drawn in AutoCAD is a pair of parallel lines with no inherent knowledge of what it represents in the physical building. The difference extends to how each platform handles design updates. Revit's model-based approach means that a floor-to-floor height change propagates to all walls, stairs, sections, and schedules automatically. AutoCAD requires the designer to locate and update each affected drawing element individually, a process that introduces error risk on complex projects. Revit's approach suits the BIM workflow standard adopted by major construction firms and project owners, while AutoCAD remains the preferred tool for detailed 2D drafting, shop drawing production, and projects where a full BIM model is not required. Is Revit Better for Building Information Modeling? Yes, Revit is a more capable platform for building information modeling. The software was built specifically around the BIM (Building Information Modeling) methodology, where a single federated model carries architectural, structural, and MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) data that all project disciplines reference and coordinate within the same environment. Revit's BIM capabilities include clash detection, which identifies physical conflicts from two building systems occupying the same space before construction begins. Quantity takeoff tools extract material volumes and counts directly from the model, supporting cost estimation and procurement. The software supports the IFC (Industry Foundation Classes) open standard for BIM data exchange, allowing Revit models to share data with structural analysis software, energy simulation tools, and facility management platforms. The clash detection and coordination capabilities of a Revit BIM model deliver measurable value compared to a disconnected set of AutoCAD drawings on large commercial projects, where coordination errors carry costs measured in hundreds of thousands of dollars. How Does AutoCAD Compare to SolidWorks in CAD Applications? AutoCAD compares to SolidWorks in CAD Applications through differences in modeling approach, design intent, and engineering focus. AutoCAD also supports 3D modeling and parametric constraints, though its core workflow remains drafting-centric, while SolidWorks is used for 3D parametric mechanical design, and the distinction reflects a fundamental difference in the types of design problems each platform is built to solve. AutoCAD's strength lies in producing precise 2D drawings for architecture, civil engineering, and electrical documentation, where flat plans and schematics are the primary deliverables. SolidWorks builds fully parametric 3D solid models where part geometry, assembly relationships, and engineering simulations are the focus. The two platforms rarely compete for the same task in practice. A mechanical engineering firm designs parts and assemblies in SolidWorks and may import 2D manufacturing drawings into AutoCAD for annotation or layout work. An architectural firm uses AutoCAD for construction document production without needing the 3D solid modeling capabilities SolidWorks provides. Choosing from these platforms depends on whether the primary output is a 2D drawing set or a 3D parametric model, and the difference is reflected in the distinct workflows that AutoCAD® vs. Solidworks® comparison analyses consistently identify. When Should You Use AutoCAD Instead of SolidWorks? AutoCAD is the appropriate choice when the primary deliverable is a 2D drawing, schematic, or layout rather than a 3D parametric model. Architectural floor plans, electrical wiring diagrams, site plans, piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), and civil road layout drawings are all produced efficiently in AutoCAD because the workflow centers on placing and annotating 2D geometry instead of constructing solid bodies. AutoCAD suits projects where imported geometry from multiple sources needs to be combined in a common drawing environment without the overhead of managing parametric feature histories. It is the preferred platform when collaborating with trades or clients whose workflows are built around DWG file exchange, a format that AutoCAD established as the industry standard for 2D drawing data. SolidWorks becomes the better choice when the project requires 3D part modeling, assembly constraint management, or integrated FEA simulation. AutoCAD delivers faster, more direct results for projects requiring only dimensioned 2D documentation without 3D geometry. Is SolidWorks Better for 3D Modeling Tasks? Yes, SolidWorks is the stronger platform for 3D modeling tasks in mechanical and product design contexts. The software provides a comprehensive parametric solid modeling environment where parts are built using feature-based history (extrusions, revolves, sweeps, lofts, fillets) that update automatically when base dimensions change. SolidWorks assembly modeling allows hundreds of parts to be mated and constrained in a virtual environment, with interference detection identifying collisions between components before physical production. Integrated simulation tools (SolidWorks Simulation) apply FEA to test stress, displacement, and safety factors on parts under defined load conditions, providing engineering data that informs geometry decisions before manufacturing begins. Sheet metal tools flatten 3D formed parts into flat patterns for laser cutting or stamping, and mold design tools create cavity and core geometry for injection molding tooling. SolidWorks provides a depth of capability that 2D-focused platforms do not match for mechanical design work requiring 3D geometry, assembly validation, and engineering analysis. How does CAD Support 3D Printing and Additive Manufacturing? CAD supports 3D printing and additive manufacturing by providing the precise digital geometry that additive manufacturing equipment requires to build physical objects layer by layer. A 3D CAD model defines the complete exterior and interior geometry of a part, including wall thicknesses, internal channels, and fine surface details, with the accuracy that printing hardware needs to produce dimensionally correct output. Most engineering additive workflows begin with CAD, but printable geometry can also originate from 3D scanning, topology optimization, or mesh sculpting tools. The CAD-to-print workflow begins with exporting the finished model as an STL or 3MF file, which converts smooth CAD geometry into a triangulated mesh that the slicing software reads. The slicer translates the mesh into layer-by-layer toolpaths at resolutions from 0.05 mm to 0.3 mm, depending on the printing technology and material. The direct digital workflow from CAD model to printed part, without intermediate machining or tooling steps, is the defining feature of 3D Printing as a manufacturing method that CAD enables from first geometry to finished component. How Are CAD Models Used in 3D Printing Processes? CAD models are used in 3D printing processes as the source geometry that defines every dimension, surface, and internal feature of the part to be printed. The model is created in CAD software with standard solid modeling tools, then exported as an STL file that represents the geometry as a mesh of triangular facets. The facet resolution controls how closely the exported mesh approximates the original smooth CAD geometry, with finer tessellation settings reducing visible facet artifacts on curved surfaces. Slicing software reads the STL file and divides the geometry into horizontal cross-sections at the layer thickness set for the print job. Each cross-section becomes a toolpath that the printer follows to deposit material, cure resin, or sinter powder. Features defined in the CAD model (holes, threads, bosses, undercuts) must meet the minimum feature size requirements of the selected printing process, which range from 0.2 mm for FDM to 0.05 mm for SLA. Dimensional accuracy from CAD model to printed part typically falls in the range of 0.1 mm to 0.5 mm, depending on machine calibration and material shrinkage. Is 3D Printing the Same As Additive Manufacturing? Yes, 3D printing is a form of additive manufacturing, and the two terms are frequently used interchangeably in both technical and commercial contexts. Additive manufacturing is the broader category that describes any process where a part is built by adding material layer by layer, as opposed to subtractive processes like milling or turning that remove material from a solid block. “3D printing” is commonly used broadly for additive manufacturing processes, including powder-bed and photopolymer systems—not just deposition-based methods and the equipment used to execute it. Additive manufacturing encompasses a wider range of technologies, including FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling), SLA (Stereolithography), SLS (Selective Laser Sintering), DMLS (Direct Metal Laser Sintering), and binder jetting, all of which qualify as additive processes. The shared principle across all additive manufacturing methods is that material is added selectively at defined coordinates derived from a CAD model, building up geometry from nothing to a finished part without the need for molds or cutting tools. What Are the Benefits and Limitations of CAD Software? The benefits and limitations of CAD Software are listed below. Precision and Accuracy : CAD software produces drawings and models with dimensional accuracy that manual drafting does not consistently achieve. Tolerances of 0.001 inches are standard in CAD-generated outputs, and mathematical geometry definitions reduce drafting and transcription errors but do not eliminate all modeling or interpretation errors that accumulate in hand-drawn work. Manufacturing processes, including CNC machining and injection molding, depend on its precision to produce parts that meet specifications on the first production run. Design Speed and Efficiency : Parametric CAD systems update associated drawings, assemblies, and documentation automatically when a single dimension changes, eliminating the manual rework that consumed significant time in pre-digital design workflows. Design cycle times in CAD-based engineering departments are 30% to 50% shorter than equivalent manual drafting processes, according to industry benchmarks across mechanical and architectural design sectors. Reusability and Standardization : CAD files are reusable across multiple projects, and standard part libraries reduce the time required to source and model frequently used components. A fastener library containing thousands of standard bolts, screws, and washers is inserted into assemblies in seconds, and company-standard title blocks, drawing templates, and layer configurations enforce consistency across an entire design department. Simulation and Validation : Integrated analysis tools within CAD software test structural integrity, thermal behavior, and fluid flow on digital models before physical prototypes are built. FEA simulations identify stress concentrations and failure points at loads from 1 lb to hundreds of thousands of pounds, allowing geometry changes to be made digitally at a fraction of the cost of physical testing. High Learning Curve : CAD software requires substantial training time before a user reaches productive proficiency. Professional-level competency in parametric modeling platforms typically requires 6 to 18 months of dedicated practice, and advanced capabilities like FEA simulation, surface modeling, and mold design add additional learning time measured in months to years. Software and Hardware Cost : Professional CAD licenses range from [$1,500 to $10,000] per seat annually for mainstream platforms, with high-end aerospace and automotive tools carrying higher costs. Hardware requirements for 3D CAD include workstation-grade graphics cards and processors, with suitable systems priced from [$2,000 to $8,000] per workstation. Cloud-based CAD subscriptions reduce upfront hardware costs but introduce ongoing subscription expenses from [$300 to $2,500] per user annually. File Compatibility Challenges : CAD files created in one platform do not always translate cleanly into another, and geometry loss or feature simplification during file conversion introduces errors that require manual correction. Translation formats (STEP, IGES, ACIS) preserve geometry but discard parametric history, limiting the editability of imported files in receiving software.

title: From Vue Storefront to Alokai: The story behind our rebranding
summary: In March 2024, Vue Storefront, a market-leading Frontend as a Service solution for composable commerce, rebranded to Alokai. Here's how the new brand came to be.
body_text: Today, we're celebrating a significant milestone in our journey – a transformative shift from Vue Storefront to Alokai. This change isn't just about a new name – it's a reflection of our growth, turning our vision into reality, and our commitment to paving the way towards composable commerce. The origin: Where did we begin? It all started when a group of developers realized there had to be a better way to optimize the Magento frontend for performance and proper customizations. The year was 2017 and the new headless approach just took on the market, promising better performance and faster delivery. So they decided to build a solution that would allow to reuse components and accelerate the development. And that’s how our open-source storefront starter came to be. Fast-forward to 2021, our journey took a significant leap and Vue Storefront came into its own, earning a spot in the Y Combinator lineup. What followed were years of product development, expanding our tech to support new backends and frameworks, securing nearly $40 million in funding, and fostering a dedicated community. Up until the very point where it's become clear that Vue Storefront has outgrown its name. Explore Alokai The change: Why are we rebranding? We grew, our customer and partner bases expanded, and now we’ve reached the point where we could no longer pretend that “Vue” and “Storefront” was enough to describe our product. "Alokai is more than a new name. This change embodies our vision to lead and guide the industry towards a future where adapting composable commerce should be as easy as possible and available to everyone. It's about embracing the full spectrum of possibilities in composable commerce, ensuring we remain at the forefront of innovation and service excellence." Patrick Friday, Alokai CEO and co-founder More than Vue, more than Storefront The announcement of our React version in March 2023 raised an important question: “They can’t seriously be running React projects with Vue literally in the name!” This moment highlighted our broader mission: to offer a true plug-and-play experience, free from the constraints of any single frontend framework or ecommerce backend. This transition reflects our journey from a specific solution to a versatile platform, ready to guide and accelerate global composable commerce and digital experiences: “Our evolution has taken us far beyond the confines of a traditional storefront. We no longer simply provide a UI kit for accelerating storefront implementation. Instead, Alokai has become a rich ecosystem of integrations, facilitating the entire customer journey – we help our clients build, connect, and deploy enterprise-grade frontends faster.” Patrick Friday, Alokai CEO and co-founder The mission: What do we hope to build? Our mission has always been clear: to guide merchants towards easier composable commerce adoption and accelerate time to market. We aim to reduce the complexity of adopting composable commerce, making it easier, faster, and more affordable for everyone. With that in mind, we give the merchants all the necessary tools to enhance their customer experience by leveraging our comprehensive platform to connect, build, deploy, and improve their online presence. "There was a clear need for a solution that would act like a bridge between complex custom code enterprises rely on and build&buy platforms with limited functionality. Alokai has become that solution.” Patrick Friday, Alokai CEO and co-founder Driving change one step at a time, frontend-first Frontend defines customer experience, which directly impacts conversion rates and revenue. But building customer experience comes with a price. Integrating different systems like CMSs, search solutions, or recommendation engines is time-consuming, expensive and requires a lot of maintenance and knowledge. Same for deploying and hosting your application later. That’s where Alokai comes in. “We are on a mission to provide one product that helps our customers to connect, build, deploy, and then improve their online stores - giving ready-made modules, like integrations with popular CMSs, but still allowing them to build their own architecture and control every part of the journey.” Filip Rakowski Alokai’s CTO and co-founder The meaning: What does Alokai stand for? In our quest for a name that captures our essence and future direction, we drew inspiration from the harmony and leadership found in an orchestra . The name Alokai is inspired by the concept of leadership and guidance, much like a conductor orchestrating a symphony. Developers are skilled musicians. The instruments are all the essential ecommerce tools: APIs, UI components, and architecture guides, etc. Each piece, from a line of code to a design element, blends like notes in a melody. And we are in the middle of it all, carefully guiding the orchestra, ensuring the symphony flows. This vision led us to 'Alakai', a term rooted in the Hawaiian language, meaning 'a leader' or 'a guide'. From this, Alokai emerged – a name that's straightforward, memorable, and perfectly reflective of our role as navigators and innovators in technology . The choice to change "a" to "o" in moving from 'Alakai' to 'Alokai' was deliberate, too, reflecting our commitment to openness and the open-source community. This subtle shift honors as well our roots in Vue Storefront, with the letter "O" being the only letter shared between the new and old name. Alokai reflects our ambition to harmonize the digital ecommerce landscape , guiding developers and businesses through the complexities of digital transformation with clarity and simplicity. “Our new identity as Alokai is a testament to our dedication to openness, innovation, and our roots in the open-source community” Patrick Friday, Alokai CEO and co-founder The change: What else is new? It’s much more than just a name, let us tell you that! Our rebranding encompasses everything from the name to the overall visual identity. The new logo and branding embody our focus on connectivity, agnosticism, and transformation. Our refreshed color palette pays homage to our origins with Vue Storefront, introducing mature shades of green, purple, and gray to symbolize our growth and evolution. But one thing will always stay the same. Our core value: Empowering developers As we live through this major update, our commitment to developers remains unchanged . Even though our focus has shifted towards serving enterprise clients, our dedication to making developers' lives easier remains at the heart of Alokai. This commitment is reflected in every line of code and page of documentation we create and share with our open-source community . The future: What’s next for Alokai? 2023 was the year when we fully embraced the spirit of agnosticism and brought to life the first truly composable frontend. This wasn't just about innovation; it was about setting a new market standard – a solution that's not tied down by frontend frameworks or backend constraints. As 2024 unfolds, we're not just stepping up; we're leaping forward! We aim to be the driving force behind the businesses stuck between “embracing risky replatforming” and “staying within the constraints of legacy systems”. Our mantra – modernize without replatforming – is more than a goal. It's a promise. “Our evolution into Alokai marks a new chapter, embodying our commitment to innovation, versatility, and developer empowerment across the globe. Looking ahead, I'm even more hopeful and excited for the future we're shaping together.” Patrick Friday, Alokai CEO and co-founder We act as a bridge between the best of MACH and legacy systems, allowing companies to remain on robust ecommerce platforms like SAP Commerce Cloud , Salesforce CC , and Adobe Commerce, while leveraging the latest composable tools at the same time. Our frontend-first approach allows merchants to introduce monumental updates with minimal changes to the user-end of things, enriching, not jeopardizing, customer experience . "Companies in composable space are obsessed with combining best-of-breed technologies as plug-and-play API's, but the frontend is still left behind. A reasonable question arises: how to maintain flexibility without being shackled by the backend technologies? At Alokai, we've tackled this head-on with our Unified Data Layer, enabling a truly decoupled frontend experience. Our approach will allow for seamless transitions and integrations, making the adoption of composable architectures less risky, more cost-effective, and truly plug-and-play.“ Filip Rakowski Alokai’s CTO and co-founder In embracing our new identity, we're not just navigating the present; we're charting a course for the future of digital commerce. A future where flexibility, speed, and innovation drive success in an ever-changing landscape. Welcome to Alokai , where we're redefining the rules, one seamless experience at a time.

body_text: Financing round co-led by EQT Life Sciences and Nextech Invest1, with participation from current and new leading global biotechnology investors Proceeds will support clinical evaluation of lead solid tumor ADC candidates, TUB-030 and TUB-040, further technology development and expansion into the US MUNICH, GERMANY, March 14, 2024 – Tubulis today announced the successful completion of an upsized and oversubscribed €128 million ($138.8 million) Series B2 financing. The round was co-led by EQT Life Sciences and Nextech Invest Ltd, on behalf of one or more funds managed by it, with participation from new US-based funds, Frazier Life Sciences and Deep Track Capital as well as all existing investors, including Andera Partners, BioMedPartners, Fund+, Bayern Kapital (with ScaleUp-Fonds Bayern), Evotec, coparion, Seventure Partners, OCCIDENT and High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF). Tubulis is developing a pipeline of uniquely matched antibody drug conjugates (ADCs) with an indication-tailored targeting molecule and payload combination to develop novel ADCs with superior properties. The proceeds of the Series B2 will primarily support progress in Tubulis’ pipeline of next-generation ADCs toward clinical evaluation and help achieve clinical proof-of-concept for lead candidates, TUB-040 and TUB-030. TUB-040 addresses tumor-antigen Napi2b, a well-characterized target in ovarian and lung cancer and TUB-030 targets 5T4, an antigen often overexpressed in solid tumors. Preclinical proof-of-concept data for these two candidates will be presented at the Annual Meeting of the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) in April. The company expects to start its first Phase 1/2a clinical trial, including dose escalation and dose optimization cohorts in 2024. The capital will also fund the expansion of Tubulis’ suite of technology platforms to unlock novel payloads for the development of versatile and customizable ADCs. In line with the addition of new US investors, Tubulis plans to increase its corporate footprint by establishing a US subsidiary. “This substantial financing from a syndicate of global specialist biotech investors recognizes Tubulis’ unique position in the ADC space. Our proprietary platform technologies and internal know-how are the foundation for our pipeline of truly differentiated protein-drug conjugates,” said Dominik Schumacher, PhD, CEO and Co-founder of Tubulis. “Our goal is to establish Tubulis as a global ADC leader as we transition into a clinical-stage company and harness the full power of ADCs to bring their therapeutic value to patients with solid tumors.” In conjunction with the financing, Christoph Broja, Managing Director at EQT Life Sciences and Kanishka Pothula, Managing Partner at Nextech Invest will join Tubulis’ Supervisory Board. An overview of all members as well as their biographies can be found on the website using the following link . Kanishka Pothula, Managing Partner at Nextech Invest commented: "Recent developments in oncology underscore the significant potential of ADCs for the treatment of solid tumors. We are convinced that Tubulis will be at the forefront of this next wave of ADC therapeutics. The team continuously pushes the boundaries of ADC design and has developed an impressive set of platform technologies that give the company the full flexibility to tailor each component of the ADC to a specific indication. The company is on the path towards providing new, high-quality treatment options for many hard-to-treat cancers and we are excited to join their journey by providing strategic support in the next phase of corporate growth.” "Dominik and the Tubulis team have developed highly differentiated ADC candidates that have the potential to significantly change the treatment paradigm in targeted solid tumor indications. We are looking forward to supporting the Tubulis team in realizing their vision of delivering the true value of ADCs by extending patient benefit and improving quality of life, said Christoph Broja, Managing Director at EQT Life Sciences. At EQT, we are focused on guiding the next global leaders in healthcare and Tubulis is well positioned to directly impact the future of oncology treatments," added John de Koning, Partner at EQT Life Sciences. Tubulis was established with the goal of maximizing the overall performance of ADCs by addressing the main bottlenecks in the field through innovation in all aspects of ADC development. The company has created a unique suite of technologies that combine a diverse range of targeting molecules, innovative payloads, and proprietary conjugation technologies to deliver revolutionary ADCs with superior, indication-tailored properties. The company's platforms allow it to move beyond traditional payload classes and expand antibody conjugation options through novel chemical groups, resulting in stable, high drug-to-antibody ratios. 1 Nextech Invest Ltd, on behalf of one or more funds managed by it.
